item.title: EXTDOC-5495:
item.content:encoded:
I agree with minmin's entire comment, including the appreciation of some of the devices used. To generalise from one criticism, I think that the implausibly poetic dialogue is just one symptom of a systemic disorder of contrivance. As another example, the needless parenthetical "illegally" and chastisement of ORIA in the main text (i.e. outside of an addendum*) felt jarringly out of place for the SCP format. Others here seem also to have noticed further instances of unsubtlety in conveying the narrative.

And this is totally aside from the writing, and I feel dumb complaining about this for two comments in a row, but the hitbox for the footnote superscripts is frustratingly small. It's not quite as bad for this as Black Highlighter–based styles, but it's still annoying.

*Thinking about it, there's something odd about the mere presence of a "conclusion" section which isn't obviously part of an addendum. I think the novelty of the CSS successfully smuggles it into the article under our noses; I'm trying to imagine it without the stylesheet, and I think it would stick out more.

item.title: SCP-5655:
item.content:encoded:
This one has a lot of issues, but lets start with the positive. I like the idea of a decomposed justice-loving Santa. But your execution leaves a lot to be desired.

Firstly, there are a couple of plot holes. There are probably millions of crimes committed in the month of December in just America alone. If this SCP showed up for every single one, the foundation would have a serious problem preventing the public from finding out about it. To fix this, perhaps you can change the article so that this scp only appears for extremely heinous crimes.

The same goes for instances where the scp shows up to give people presents. The scp showing up to give people presents could result in the public finding out about anomalies. The foundation needs a way to prevent the public from finding out, so either remove this bit or add a way for the scp foundation to track the scp so they can amnesticize individuals who were exposed.

The concepts also leaves a lot of unanswered questions. For instance, can the scp be in two places at once? If a bunch of people commit a crime at the same time but in different places, will the scp appear for only one person, or will a manifestation of the scp appear for all of the people.

Another question is if people have to "fix their unlawful act" for the scp to leave them alone, what counts as fixing an unlawful act. If you murdered someone, would you need to find a way to bring the person you murdered back to life. You need to create a specific set of rules that can be applied universally.

Additionally, you never specify what powers the scp has. Can it teleport? What if you try to fight it while the scp is trying to disembowel you. Does it have a way to immobilize its targets through combat or an afflicted paralysis? That needs to be specified.

Finally, why do people exposed to the scp need to be killed if any unlawful act can summon the scp? That seems excessive and inefficient, which is why the foundation wouldn't do it. It seems more likely that the foundation would investigate what those individuals did and determine and appropriate response. Additionally, why does the tree as well as the dishes/containers for the milk and cookies need to be incinerated. You said that was to prevent contamination, but I thought the scp only affected individuals who did unlawful acts. Is the scp diseased or something?

Overall, there are lots of unanswered questions and glaring plot holes.

There are also lots of issues with you grammar scattered throughout the article. I'm not going to list them all since this is already a long post, but one example is in the very first sentence, where you use "is" when you should use "are". There are several other mistakes like this throughout the article

You also have a bad habit of making your sentences to long by writing in a very indirect and convoluted way. For instance, you wrote:

"SCP 5655 will manifest nearby an individual who has committed an unlawful act in the duration of the month December."

The first issue is that you tend to use a conjugation of "is" before every verb in this sentence (manifest and commit). You shouldn't do that sparingly at most. It would be better like this:

"SCP 5655 manifests near individuals who commit unlawful acts in the duration of the month December."

Another way to cut down on fluff is at the very end of that sentence, where you wrote "in the duration of the month of December". That can be shortened to "during the month of December", giving us the final edited version of that sentence:

"SCP 5655 manifests near individuals who commit unlawful acts during the month December."

Writing it like this is clearer and more concise. Most of you sentences have issues like this, which makes the overall article sound unprofessional. That takes away from the immersion of the entry, since the foundation is supposed to be all about cold professionalism.

item.content:encoded:
Howdy hey

Remember: The main site is for summary judgment of final work, not feedback and critique on unfinished work.

Readers are not required to review your articles since the site is for finished works only. It was your responsibility to receive critique by our IRC Chats or our idea critique forums.
